title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: Grothendieck is axiomatising the profinite groups of 'arithmetic fundamental group' type, which he calls 'LT-groupes'. There is an extension of profinite groups 1 → Π → M → N → 1, where Π is a profinite group with a distinguished structure (a geometric fundamental group). There is also a 'torus' K: T ↪ Π, with T ≅ Ẑ(1) and image L = K(T), a procyclic inertia or loop subgroup. Let N(L) = Norm_M(L). Then N(L)/L acts on L ≅ Ẑ through a 'cyclotomic character' that is induced by a character χ_N: N → Ẑ*.

This page:
1. The essential hypothesis is that χ_N(N), and hence χ(N(L)/L), is an open subgroup of Ẑ*. The image of N(L)/L in N is open, so the second statement follows from the first.
2. The hypothesis is intrinsic to M and does not depend on the choice of Π. The reason is that M carries an intrinsically defined cyclotomic character χ_M: M → Ẑ* (18). The hypothesis just says that χ_M(M) is open.
3. Consequence (19): every open subgroup of N(L)/L acts non-trivially on L. Its χ-image is open in Ẑ*, so it contains elements ≠ 1, and such an element acts on L ≅ Ẑ by multiplication by a non-trivial unit.
4. 'By the standard arguments' (the next page makes this explicit) this implies an abstract monodromy theorem. Take any field K, notably an ℓ-adic field Q_ℓ, any affine group scheme G of finite type over K, and any homomorphism u: M → G(K). Then u restricted to L is quasi-unipotent: some open L' ⊂ L maps to unipotent elements. Equivalently, a power of u(generator) is unipotent.
5. The standard argument (Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem) runs as follows. If σ ∈ N(L) and σ l σ⁻¹ = l^{χ(σ)}, then the eigenvalues of u(l) are stable under λ ↦ λ^{χ(σ)}. Choose χ(σ) of infinite order (in the ℓ-adic case, a non-root-of-unity in Z_ℓ*). This forces the eigenvalues to be roots of unity.

The purpose is to isolate, purely in group-theoretic terms, the property of 'arithmetic' profinite groups that yields quasi-unipotent local monodromy. This is part of the anabelian programme of the Longue Marche.
errors: Continuity of u is not stated. For K finitely generated over Q with the discrete topology, a continuous u has finite image, so the claim is trivial. The meaningful case is K ℓ-adic with u continuous (or u factoring through an ℓ-adic image).

Openness of χ alone is not quite what the eigenvalue argument uses: it needs, for the relevant ℓ, an element whose χ-value has infinite order in Z_ℓ*. This does follow from openness, but it is not spelled out.
The step from openness of χ_N(N) to openness of χ(N(L)/L) relies on the parenthetical claim that the image of N(L)/L in N is open. That claim is asserted as 'easy' but is not proved.

ideas.what: Intrinsic cyclotomic character χ_M: M → Ẑ* of an abstract 'LT-group', with the arithmeticity hypothesis 'image open in Ẑ*'
ideas.modern_name: cyclotomic character of a profinite group of arithmetic (GC/anabelian) type; group-theoretic reconstruction of the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche, 1981); later made precise in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi and others)
ideas.where_published: Ideas related to the Longue Marche and the Esquisse d'un programme; this exact formulation is unsure

ideas.what: The normaliser of an inertia (torus) subgroup acts on it through the cyclotomic character; every open subgroup acts non-trivially
ideas.modern_name: inertia/cusp subgroups and their normalisers (decomposition groups) in arithmetic fundamental groups

ideas.what: Quasi-unipotence of the restriction to L of any homomorphism into G(K), deduced from non-trivial cyclotomic conjugation action
ideas.where_published: Serre–Tate, Good reduction of abelian varieties (1968), appendix; SGA 7 I, exposé I

missed.claim: The monodromy theorem is formulated axiomatically for abstract profinite 'LT-groups' with an intrinsic cyclotomic character, independent of any geometric origin. Openness of the cyclotomic image is identified as the key intrinsic hypothesis. This is an early group-theoretic packaging of a known argument, not a new result.
missed.quote: Cette hypothèse a une signification intrinsèque (en termes du LT-groupe M lui-même — indépendamment du choix de Π)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a minor historical precursor to the group-theoretic reconstruction of cyclotomic characters and inertia in anabelian geometry. It is mathematically routine.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an axiomatic restatement of Grothendieck's own published quasi-unipotence argument inside the 'LT-group' framework of the Longue Marche. It is of mild historical interest only and contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: The parenthesis after 'corps K' reads '(notamment un corps ℓ-adique Q_ℓ)', not '(extension d'un corps de type fini sur Q)'.
'(en termes du LT-groupe M lui-même — indépendamment du choix de Π)': the choice is of Π (capital), not π.

'Revenant à L et N(L), on voit que l'hypothèse faite implique ceci' is correct; '(19) Tout sous-groupe ouvert de N(L)/L opère non trivialement sur L' (the struck word 'sur' is replaced by 'sur' again, effectively 'opère non trivialement sur L').
'On sait, par les arguments standards que ceci implique que pour tout corps K' — 'standards' confirmed.
